question: What is the main job of the nephrons in the kidneys?

options.A: Transporting urine directly to the urethra
options.B: Storing urine until it leaves the body
options.C: Pumping blood through the lower back
options.D: Filtering the blood to form urine

explanation: You've got this! Nephrons are the tiny working units inside your kidneys that clean your blood and make urine. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h1)

question: What is the main difference between the ureters and the urethra?

options.A: Ureters store urine, while the urethra filters waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: Ureters and urethra perform the exact same task on opposite sides of the pelvis
options.C: Ureters carry urine from kidneys to the bladder, while the urethra carries urine outside the body
options.D: Ureters pump urine out of the body, while the urethra connects the kidneys directly to the outside

explanation: Think of ureters as the pipes coming down from the kidneys to the bladder, and the urethra as the final exit tube to the outside world! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h1)

question: What do we call pain or a burning feeling when passing urine?
explanation: Dysuria is just the medical word for painful or burning urination. Great term to keep in your clinical vocabulary bag! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h2)

question: A patient suddenly feels a strong need to pee and leaks a little before reaching the toilet. What is this called?
explanation: Incontinence simply means losing control of urine flow. You will see this a lot in clinical rotations! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h2)

question: When checking for urinary retention, what does a nurse feel for in the lower belly?

options.A: A firm, rounded bladder above the pubic bone
options.B: Soft, empty folds of skin near the belly button
options.C: Warm fluid moving freely inside the intestines
options.D: A hard, pulsing mass on the left side

explanation: When urine gets trapped (retention), the bladder fills up and feels like a firm dome right above the pubic bone. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why do doctors order a urine culture after a test shows an infection?

options.A: To find the exact type of bacteria and the best antibiotic to treat it
options.B: To check if the kidneys are filtering red blood cells properly
options.C: To measure the exact total volume of urine produced in twenty-four hours
options.D: To scan the bladder walls for structural tears or tumors

explanation: A regular test tells us there's an infection, but a culture helps us pick the exact right drug to knock it out! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h3)

question: Tracking a patient's fluid intake and output mainly helps you evaluate what?

options.B: Muscle strength in the lower limbs

explanation: Checking what goes in versus what comes out is a brilliant way to see if the kidneys are doing their job and if the patient is well-hydrated. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h4)

question: A patient on a bedpan is struggling to urinate while lying flat. What should you try first?

options.A: Assist the patient into a more natural, upright sitting position
options.B: Restrict all fluid intake for the rest of the day
options.C: Insert an indwelling catheter immediately without further delay
options.D: Administer a strong diuretic medication by mouth

explanation: Gravity and a normal sitting posture help relax the muscles, making it much easier to pass urine naturally. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h4)

question: Where should a urinary drainage bag always hang relative to the patient's bladder?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Flat on the floor next to the bed
options.C: Above the level of the bladder

explanation: Always keep it lower than the bladder! Gravity keeps the urine flowing away from the body and stops nasty germs from creeping back up. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of these is unsafe when caring for a patient with an indwelling catheter?

options.A: Keeping the drainage bag below the level of the bladder
options.B: Cleaning the perineal area and catheter tubing daily
options.C: Disconnecting the tubing frequently to let the patient walk easier
options.D: Removing the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed

explanation: Never break that closed system! Opening the tubing lets bacteria waltz right into the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is the main goal of teaching Kegel exercises to someone with urinary incontinence?

options.A: To strengthen the pelvic floor muscles supporting the bladder
options.B: To relax the abdominal wall during a physical exam
options.C: To stretch the ureters and widen the urinary tract
options.D: To increase total daily urine production in the kidneys

explanation: Kegels tone up those pelvic floor muscles, giving the patient much better control over when they go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h6)

question: How does bladder retraining help a patient with urge incontinence?

options.A: It numbs the bladder nerves permanently using special exercises
options.B: It trains the bladder to hold increasing amounts of urine by voiding on a set timetable
options.C: It empties the bladder continuously so the patient never feels any sensation
options.D: It stops the kidneys from producing urine during the night hours

explanation: Following a set bathroom schedule helps calm the bladder down and slowly helps it hold more urine over time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h6)
